Collective Worship
At St Martin’s CE Primary School, our daily act of collective worship is an integral part of the day. It provides us with an opportunity to gather as a school community to reflect, think and pray. During collective worship, we reflect on our school values and promote the spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of our children.
Collective worship is led by a range of people over the week: the Senior Leadership Team, Rev Rosy, Sing Academy, class teachers, and the children.
Monday – Collective Worship led by the Worship Leaders and a senior leader
Tuesday – Collective Worship led by Reverend Rosy

Our Faith
Welcome to St. Martin's>>
Our Faith>>
Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven. Matthew 5:16
St Martin’s CE Primary School provides a happy, nurturing and supportive environment rooted in the principles of the Christian faith; this allows children to grow and flourish, both spiritually and morally. All members of our school community are valued and respected, so that everyone develops a positive attitude towards themselves, others and the community.
Our school’s Christian character contributes significantly to the academic achievement, personal development and well-being of all learners. Although we are a church school, we are inclusive with all members of the community we serve. Our aim is that pupils of all faiths and those without a faith feel safe and happy, secure in the knowledge that their beliefs are respected and valued.
St. Martin’s core values are at the very heart of our school. Our values are derived from key values central to Christianity. We are ambitious – we want each member of the school to flourish and realise their true potential in a nurturing Christian environment.
A deeply Christian ethos runs through the school, serving the common good. All members of school feel supported and valued. Our school is a place where relationships flourish and grow; relationships within the whole community are important, not only amongst the staff and children but also with the wider community.

Promoting British Values
Promoting British Values>>
Promoting British Values
At St Martin’s CofE Primary School, we provide opportunities for pupils to explore their own culture and have a clear understanding and appreciation of a wide range of cultural influences that have shaped modern Britain. We encourage all children to be tolerant and respectful to those of different faiths and beliefs. This is done by providing the children with an understanding of main festivals and key dates of significant to British culture. e.g. Remembrance Day, the Queen’s Birthday and major political events such as elections.
We ‘promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs’. We also recognise that these values are not solely exclusive to Britain and that these values have developed in Britain through a process over a substantial period of time and can only be maintained and developed by active engagement of citizens in democratic, lawful and respectful institutions and processes, of which our Primary School is one element.
Democracy
Children, parents and Staff have many opportunities for their voices to be heard at St Martin’s.
An obvious example of democracy in action is our School Council, each year, the election of School Council members takes place. This reflects our British electoral system; the prospective candidates make speeches; all pupils reflect on what personal characteristics are important for their class representatives to have.
Following this they vote and the individuals with the majority are elected. In the past the school Council has decided on playground equipment for both indoor and outdoor, and have given feedback to curriculum leaders on the curriculum.
Other examples of how we promote the values of democracy, including ‘pupil voice’ are:
Children agree the school values
Rule of Law
The importance of laws, whether they may be those of each class, the school, or our country are referred to and reinforced, such as through Worship and when reflecting on behaviour choices. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind decisions, and the consequences if they are broken.
This is reinforced in different ways:
Collective Worship covers national and International events
Individual Liberty
Within School, Pupils are actively encouraged to make choices; including the right to respectfully express views and beliefs, knowing they are in a safe and supportive environment.
We promote individual Liberty through:
Choices about learning activities and challenges
Building Learning power
Opportunities to reflect, in their reflection books
Mutual Respect
Mutual respect is at the heart of what we believe. Children learn that their actions have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community should treat each other with respect.
We promote this through:
PSHCE and Circle Time sessions
Anti-bullying activities
RE curriculum
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and beliefs
St Martin’s has a diverse community and as such we place emphasis on sharing and promoting this diversity
As well as promoting British Values, we would actively challenge pupils, staff, or parents expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British values including ‘extremist views’.

Welcome to St. Martin's
Welcome to St. Martin's>>
Message from the Headteacher
Welcome to St Martin’s CE Primary School. It is my pleasure to welcome you to our school. Our school, serving the West Drayton community, is proud to be a Church of England school rooted in the teachings of Jesus and inspired by Martin of Tours. Our school vision — “Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven” (Matthew 5:16) — guides everything we do. We are committed to nurturing courageous, compassionate children who flourish academically, spiritually and socially.
St Martin’s is a warm, inclusive Christian community where we celebrate the dignity and worth of every child. Our Christian values of compassion, trust, prayer and generosity are lived out daily across classrooms, worship and community life. We welcome families of all backgrounds and beliefs and are committed to inclusive practice so every child can shine. As a primary school moving to one form entry and part of LDBS Frays Academy Trust, we also run a special resource provision for 12 children (The Lighthouse). Located in West Drayton, we know our community well and because of this we are determined to provide high-quality, compassionate education for every family we serve.
We are proud of the outcomes of our recent inspections which reflect our commitment to high standards and to caring for the whole child. Our SIAMS inspection noted that “the school’s Christian character enables pupils to flourish; leaders and governors are committed to ensuring that the distinctiveness and effectiveness of the Church school are sustained.” Ofsted commented that “pupils are supported well and make positive progress. Leaders know the community well and provide a strong, caring ethos for pupils and families.” These findings align with our ongoing priorities: safeguarding, inclusive provision, curriculum quality, and strong leadership and governance, and we use our understanding the needs of our chidren and community to shape our continuous improvement.
At St Martin’s you can expect a rich curriculum that is carefully sequenced and adapted to meet the needs of all learners, including those with SEND and those supported through our special resource provision. We combine high expectations for academic progress with strong pastoral care rooted in Christian values: worship, reflection and opportunities to serve the local community. We set clear expectations for behaviour, attendance and personal development so every child can thrive academically and morally. Families can expect dedicated staff, clear communication and close partnerships to help children realise their God-given potential.
Daily life at St Martin’s includes collective worship and reflection where children explore values such as generosity and courage and put them into practice. Children enjoy outdoor learning activities that build resilience, teamwork and curiosity. We provide tailored interventions and specialist support for children with additional needs, working closely with parents and external agencies. We celebrate pupil achievement in lessons, assemblies and community events, showcasing good deeds and positive impact.
We are committed to governance, transparency and strong community partnership. As part of our responsibilities we publish up-to-date governance information and ensure transparency about leadership arrangements and how we use resources to benefit pupils. Our governing body and the trust work closely with leaders to ensure accountability and continual improvement.
Practical information: our admissions arrangements and details of how we manage in-year applications are available on our website and through the trust; please contact the school office for current application guidance. We warmly welcome prospective parents and carers to visit, see our school in action and meet staff and pupils. Follow our news and events to see how our vision and values are lived out — from sports days and performances to community outreach.
At St Martin’s we believe every child is a beacon of potential. Our Christian ethos and commitment to inclusion ensure that children are known, valued and supported to succeed. We look forward to partnering with you as we help your child flourish academically, spiritually and personally. Contact the school office to arrange a visit or to request further information about admissions and our provision.
St Martin’s C.E Primary School

PE and Sport Premium>>
Sports Premium Grant
The government has been providing additional funding of £150 million per annum for academic years 2016-2017 through to 2020 to improve the provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools.
This funding – provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport – will be allocated to primary school headteachers. This funding is ring-fenced and therefore can only be spent on the provision of PE and sport in schools.
The purpose of this funding is to spend the additional funding on improving the provision of PE and sport within schools. Headteachers have the freedom to choose how this will be implemented within their school. Our attached PE and Sports Premium Statement will inform you how we are spending this funding.
How this funding is being used at St Martin’s C E Primary School:
This year St Martin’s C E Primary School will receive a sports premium amount of £17,178. This will be paid to us in the autumn term.
At St Martin’s C E Primary School we feel it is important to encourage pupils to lead healthy and active lifestyles. We have therefore decided to spend this year’ funding on directly increasing participation in sport and extending sporting opportunities. The funding will be spent on:
How will we monitor the impact of this funding:
The school will be monitoring both the physical development & engagement levels of pupils through teacher observation and an assessment system and quality assurance measures.
The school will be offering a variety of after school sports clubs and will be closely monitoring the attendance to ensure maximum take up.

Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care>>
Breakfast Club
To ensure that pupils have the best possible start to their day, we provide a Breakfast Club at St. Martin’s School. Our Breakfast Club is run by school staff in the lunch hall. It runs Monday to Friday, starting at 8:00am and finishing at 8.45am, with last admission at 8.30am. Children are taken to their classes before registration.
The children can choose from a range of food items, including cereal, toast, a range of fruit and juices.
A range of activities are on offer to keep the children engaged and for them to enjoy.
In order to attend, you must pay £2 via ParentPay.
Pupils will need to book and pay for a place in advance but can come as often as they like.
Join us for a great start to the school day!
If you are interested in attending the Breakfast Club, please register your interest by contacting the school office at: stmartins@fraysacademytrust.org
After-School Club
The provider of the After School Club is School Friends.
The club is open to children from Reception to Year 6 and will run Monday to Friday, 3:00–6:00pm. Think fun-packed afternoons filled with games, crafts, friendships, and happy moments all in a safe, inclusive, and caring environment. Oh, and did we mention the yummy healthy snacks included in our fees to keep everyone energised?
If you want to book your child a place, please click here.
Session Fees:Please click here to be taken to their website.
After-school sports clubs are run by our PE provider, PSD. These take place on a Monday, Thursday and Friday after, from 15:20–16:15.
At the beginning of each term, the school will email parents with the clubs and times - if you would like your child to be part of a club, then you will need to email the school back. If your child is successful, you will be notified via email.
If your child is unsuccessful, their name will be held on a waiting list: you will then be contacted if a place becomes available.
Clubs will not run in the first and last weeks of term.

The Lighthouse: Specialist Resource Provision>>
Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven. Matthew 5:16
SRP – What we offer
Who are we, and what are our skills?
Within the SRP we have well-qualified and experienced staff. The provision for children in the SRP is led by the SENCO and monitored by the senior leadership team.
What services can my child access?
There are a variety of different services that are available to children in SRP. These include:
How will you help my child transition into your provision?
We use a range of strategies to support your child in their transition to The SRP.
What do you teach my child?
The children will be taught an individualised curriculum, focusing on:
Children will also access differentiated mainstream school curriculum opportunities including, Literacy, Numeracy, Science, ICT etc.
Children will access mainstream classes for some of this teaching dependent on their individual needs and targets set within their EHC Plans.
How would the curriculum be adapted to support my child?
We assess the child through observations and assessment for learning strategies as part of our daily teaching practice.
We also track their progress termly.
How do you communicate with parents?
We communicate with parents via:
If parents are not available to talk to staff during the school staff's working hours, we will communicate using a home/school communication book.
Occupational Therapy
Speech and Language Therapy
Access to the Education Psychologist
Visits to their current school
Discussions with current teachers
Admission interviews with parents
A home visit where appropriate
Individual transition plan
Learning and life skills
Communication
Social Skills
Interaction
Interpersonal Skill
Behaviour expectations
Phone Calls
Feedback
How do we support pupils with SEN to improve their emotional and social development?
St Martin’s School is a place where children thrive socially, emotionally and academically. We are an inclusive school; we welcome and celebrate diversity. All staff believe that children having high self-esteem is crucial to a child’s well-being. We have a caring, understanding team looking after our children who feel safe, happy and valued as individuals.
• The class teacher has overall responsibility for the pastoral, medical and social care of children in their class. Therefore, this would be the parents’ first point of contact. If further support is required, the class teacher would liaise with the SENDCo for further advice and support. This may involve working alongside outside agencies. For example: Health and Social Services, CFACs and Educational Psychologists.
• Our school is a safe place for children to attend. It has a caring ethos and prioritises the safeguarding of all children at all times. The safety and safeguarding of our children is of the utmost importance. Please refer to our Frays Child Protection Policy and Anti-Bullying Policy for more information.
